locus: §3.1 — “Prevalence is only meaningful against a measured false-positive rate”
current:
Prevalence is only meaningful against a measured false-positive rate.
**Specificity is measured in-domain at two grains at once**: each chamber
carries its own 60-segment pre-AI control — a check that chamber-specific
editorial registers do not manufacture false positives — while the pooled

against semi-synthetic ground truth; and commercial-detector exercises have
leaned on a single fifty-speech calibration or on vendor benchmarks alone.
Twenty-one chambers with in-domain controls each is the same idea carried
to the grain this corpus allows.
proposed:
Prevalence is meaningful only against a measured false-positive rate. We measure specificity in-domain at two grains. Each chamber has its own 60-segment pre-AI control, testing whether chamber-specific editorial registers manufacture false positives; the pooled 1,260 provides the statistical weight (§4.1). The per-chamber controls test heterogeneity rather than establish independent specificity estimates: no 60/60 cell is treated as sufficient on its own.

This design differs from the published comparators (§5). The closest parliamentary study measures false positives on one pre-LLM hold-out in each of two parliaments. Population-level studies validate by venue against semi-synthetic ground truth, while commercial-detector exercises have relied on a single fifty-speech calibration or vendor benchmarks alone. Here, 21 chambers each contribute an in-domain control, carrying the same calibration principle to the grain the corpus allows.
rationale: The revision removes self-evaluative claims (“single most important,” “exceeds the field's practice”) and lets the concrete comparison establish the design's contribution. It also separates the statistical role of the pooled sample from the heterogeneity role of chamber controls.
